subject: Measurement contract, prompt retention & technical acceptance criteria - follow-up
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@nemara.com>, Chris O'Connell <chris.oconnell@fastretail.co>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Measurement contract, prompt retention & technical acceptance criteria - follow-up

Jamie / Chris — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can lock the qualification timeline and measurement contract.

Key outcomes from the call:
- FastRetail is targeting a production-quality SLO for chat-based checkout assistance (streaming + end-of-turn).
- Target geography: US east / multi-AZ.
- Primary KPIs: latency (streaming tail), per-session throughput, and stable concurrency for sustained peaks.
- Nemara (FastRetail) wants reproducible benchmark artifacts and a signed measurement contract before procurement moves forward.

Action items (owners & ETA):
1) Redwood to propose a Measurement Contract draft and prompt retention policy — Priyom / Marissa — by EOD tomorrow (2026-09-24).
2) Technical acceptance criteria (latency & concurrency buckets, measurement method) — Marissa / Karthik — provide a 1-page spec and test harness link by 2026-09-24 12:00 PT.
3) Customer to confirm representative prompt-set and traffic mix (50% streaming session flows, 30% non-streaming long-form completions, 20% rerank) — Jamie — by 2026-09-25.
4) Procurement and legal to review measurement contract after internal sign-off — Chris to loop in procurement contact.

Notes on scope we proposed verbally (please confirm in reply):
- Latency SLO targets are draft only; final values in the Measurement Contract. Redwood expects to run canonical runs using the supplied prompt pack + our eval harness.
- We will preserve prompt provenance and a hashed prompt archive (prompt retention) and provide a reproducibility recipe (seeded runs, container image).

Attachments included: initial prompt pack (sample rows) and a measurement_contract_v1 placeholder (PDF stub) for internal review.

If that aligns, we can schedule the reproducibility run (48-hour run window) as soon as the contract is signed.

Thanks — Priyom

--
Priyom Das
Solutions Lead, Performance & Qualification
Redwood Inference
priom@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@nemara.com>

Cc: Chris O'Connell <chris.oconnell@fastretail.co>
Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 17:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Measurement contract, prompt retention & technical acceptance criteria - follow-up

Priyom — thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from our side before we finalize the prompt pack: 

1) Streaming expectations: for real-time checkout we need p95 chunk-to-client delta < 120ms for incremental tokens under typical network conditions. We realize server-side smoothing may add a small margin; please indicate whether this needs to be a p95 or p99 SLO in your draft.
2) Concurrency: peak concurrent sessions expected 4k for Black Friday bounded bursts; steady-state concurrency 500. We need the benchmark to show behavior across both modes.
3) Prompt retention: for compliance we can provide the prompt set but only allow hashed provenance in public artifacts. Is that acceptable?

We will confirm the official representative prompt sample by 2026-09-25. Also looping in procurement (Chris) to confirm timing for contract review and any PO constraints.

—Jamie
Principal PM, Checkout Experience
FastRetail / Nemara Group
jamie.liu@nemara.com | +1 (646) 555-0912

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Jamie Liu <jamie.liu@nemara.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 24 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Measurement contract, prompt retention & technical acceptance criteria - follow-up

Jamie — thanks, this is helpful. Below is the technical acceptance criteria draft (one-page summary) we mentioned on the call. I've attached the full prompt pack CSV sample and the Measurement Contract PDF stub for legal/procurement to preview.

TECHNICAL ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA (draft)
- Workloads: representative mix supplied by customer (by percent): streaming session flows (50%), non-streaming long completions (30%), rerank requests (20%).
- Latency (non-streaming): p95 token-generation latency <= 350ms for requests up to 512 tokens; p99 <= 700ms.
- Latency (streaming): p95 chunk-to-client delta <= 150ms on our lab WAN profile; customers may request p95 <= 120ms as a tighter target — we can include an appendix with measurement notes.
- Throughput/Concurrency buckets (Sustained 10-minute windows): 
  - Steady: concurrency 500, min sustained throughput 5k tokens/sec cluster-wide.
  - Peak: concurrency 4k (burst), system should not degrade below 80% successful streaming sessions.
- Reproducibility: all runs executed with: fixed seed for sampling, recorded model hash & quantization profile, container image digest, and the same harness binary. We will publish a run recipe and a Docker image tag; prompt originals remain on customer-controlled storage.
- Measurement harness: Redwood's benchmark harness (link in attachments) will: orchestrate warmup, simulate realistic network jitter, generate per-token timing, and produce an artifact bundle (raw trace, aggregated SLOs, and a reproducibility manifest).
- Acceptance check: customer review of artifact bundle + cross-check of seeded repeat run (within +/- 5% of baseline for throughput & p95 latency).

Notes on prompt retention and compliance:
- For PII or regulated prompts, customer provides prompts into a secure staging bucket. Redwood will store only a hashed index and the reproducibility manifest in our run artifact. Detailed prompt retention policy is included in the Measurement Contract (see PDF).

Next steps (as promised):
- Priyom and I will finalize Measurement Contract text today and share a DocuSign link.
- Karthik will drop a short guide to running the harness locally and the canonical command-line flags. (Link included.)
- Once the prompt pack is confirmed by FastRetail, we will schedule a 48-hour reproducibility window and export artifacts for joint review.

Attachments in this email:
- benchmark_prompt_pack_v1.csv (sample rows, 120 prompts) [attachment: benchmark_prompt_pack_v1.csv (text/csv)]
- measurement_contract_v1.pdf [attachment: measurement_contract_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]
- harness_run_recipe.md (drive link) https://drive.google.com/open?id=1QxBenchmarkPack

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com | +1 (650) 555-0199

Also, timeline looks good. Proposed timeline:
- 9/24: Redwood finalizes contract draft + DocuSign link.
- 9/25: FastRetail provides representative prompt subset (hashed + secure bucket).
- 9/27-9/29: Redwood runs reproducibility tests (48-hour window within this range).
- 10/2: Joint artifact review and post-run remediation plan if SLOs aren't met.

Procurement contact: Lori Mendes (lori.mendes@fastretail.co) — she will be on the doc for legal redlines.

If you can add the 30-day holdback clause language and re-issue the DocuSign link today, we can move quickly.

Thanks — Chris
